nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Ruby Walker's kitchen. A pine table under the window, a heater beside it. This is where the four sat with Violet's letter, week after week.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Before the letter, it was Tuesdays. Violet came for years, and Ruby had the heater on before she knocked.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: Heater on, her at the door, then the same argument we'd had for years. That was the friendship. Tea?

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: The argument was about whether Ruby's husband should be told. Told what?

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: You came for Violet, not my marriage. Leave him out of it. Anyway, tea?

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Ruby kept her copy of the note. Four went out, all the same, two weeks after Violet died. I photographed hers at the kitchen table. It is under glass on my board now, in Violet's handwriting.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: If you've got this, I'm dead, and I'm sorry about the timing. Go to my locker at the boatsheds by the slip. The padlock's new and these four keys are the only ones. Go together, all four of you, and read what's there together. Violet.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: That's all of it.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: It isn't any of you four, and I'd know. Someone with my key has been in my house, or I've started imagining things. I can't tell which, and both frighten me.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: The first thing was the yard gate. I bolt it every night. One morning in October it was unbolted, and I couldn't swear I'd bolted it.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: I changed the front door lock and told only you four where the new spare was. It happened again after that. So I took the key in, told nobody, and it stopped.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: I don't think I'm going to die. I think I'm going to be sixty and embarrassed. If I'm wrong, nobody needs to know. If I'm right, you'll want to know what I noticed.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Here Ruby's hand goes over the page. The lines about Violet's mother. She picks up again below her hand.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: Somebody got the place of my spare from one of you without your knowing, or watched one of you use it. Write down everything odd you've noticed this year. About me, and about who has been near each of you.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: Read the four lists together at one table. Since I'm asking you to, here's mine. Liam has owned a third of the yard for eight years and lets the town think he's staff.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Her hand goes down again. One line. She won't read that one either.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: Ruby's been on nights since August and won't say why. Margo hasn't been to the slip since summer. And Brad paid me back the van money this autumn, every penny. The one thing this year that went right.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: Not the police. I've nothing they'd act on, and I won't have them in your lives over a gate and a feeling. You four can do what they won't. Read this together. Be careful. Write legibly. Violet.

decision.prompt: What does the city hear next week?

options.label: Air Ruby's whole reading
options.result: I'll air every line Ruby read. The words go out in Ruby's voice as much as Violet's, and Ruby carries them round Havenbay.

options.label: Air only verified lines
options.result: I'll air only lines I can verify elsewhere. The city hears less, and what Ruby covered stays at her table.

after.speaker: Ruby Walker
after.line: If you cut what I read, people will think I cut it. The lines under my hand stay there either way.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Ruby Walker is in her mid thirties, a practice nurse at the surgery on Wharf Street.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: You're talking about me like I'm not in the room.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: When she is frightened, she talks. She fills the room, gives you a job and makes tea nobody asked for.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: Six years sober. The glass is tonic. Say that too, before somebody else decides what it is.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Ruby gave me this memory without being asked.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: Three years ago Vi rang me at four in the morning. I drove over. Neither of us ever said what it was, not that night and not after. Anyway.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: I don't know what happened. Ruby did not say, and I am not going to guess.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: When we opened the locker, the first thing was relief. Then shame, because relief meant we'd believed she might name one of us.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: The next evening you did the arithmetic.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: New lock. Only four told. Something moved after. Key taken in, it stopped. Liam found the pot empty, broke a pane, and the back door was latched.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: But the wall could be climbed. Someone could have watched Violet use the pot.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: I know. We looked outward: no cleaner, lodger or tradesman, and an estranged sister. Then Monday: me on shift, Margo home, Liam at the yard, Brad at home. Nobody had an alibi. Liam had the least.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: When Brad's rent stopped, his landlord boxed up the flat and sent everything to Ruby. Police had already searched it.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Ruby and I went through the boxes over days. Passport, cards, tools, laptop, clothes and paperwork. Days of careful nothing.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: He'd put his keys on the table, then move them. Twice, always twice. We used to wait for the second move before we spoke.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: He said thank you like it cost him. He was up at five to run, and he agreed with whoever had spoken last. Seven years he was the pet of the room.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Four ordinary habits, remembered with affection. That was Brad Collins as Ruby had him.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Ruby kept the envelope her note came in. Folded behind the note was a covering slip from Violet's solicitor.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: It says the four envelopes were lodged with the firm three weeks before Violet died and posted after the funeral.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: Four addressees. Liam, me, Margo, Brad. I've read that list enough times to know the order.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: The letter was dated three weeks before Violet died. Police examined it, then returned it to Ruby.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: Every Saturday we came back to this table with the lists Violet asked for. Every Saturday Liam looked worse.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: The line about the police. Did that sound like Violet to you?

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: Never. Liam said that night why she was like that about them. Something from the night her mum died. I let it go. Then the facts bent towards him: the yard, the lines about her mother, the bedroom window, the back door.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Each of those could also be a friend helping a friend. Brad kept saying so.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: Every week. Reasonably. He lost every week. By the fifth we'd settled on Liam. At the sixth Margo stopped arguing and looking at anyone. A week later Brad drove to Kestrel Head. She thought she'd know, and she's dead. Anyway.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: This week Ruby Walker read me Violet's letter at the table where the four worked it.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: By the fifth Saturday the room had settled on Liam. At the sixth Margo went quiet. A week later Brad drove to Kestrel Head.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Brad Collins, as Ruby had him: keys moved twice on the table, thank you like it cost him, up at five to run, and he agreed with whoever spoke last.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Next week I air Ruby's whole reading. This is Echoes of Havenbay, I'm Ally Quinn. Goodnight for now, Harbour. Sleep tight.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Next week I air only verified lines. What Ruby covered stays at her table. This is Echoes of Havenbay, I'm Ally Quinn. Goodnight for now, Harbour. Sleep tight.
